fields.narrative_intro: *A ravenous person and a melodramatic person discuss GitHub Copilot Autofix at a 3am Walmart.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
RAVENOUS PERSON: "Snowflake shipped Copilot's Autofix to fix security holes."
MELODRAMATIC PERSON: "Finally, AI protecting us from ourselves."
fields.panel2:
[build]
RAVENOUS PERSON: "PR #1218, merged June 18th. Looked totally clean."
MELODRAMATIC PERSON: "Beautiful. A golden age of safe code."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
RAVENOUS PERSON: "It swapped a safe jq pattern for raw issue title interpolation."
MELODRAMATIC PERSON: "...Autofix autobroke it?"
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The melodramatic person's arms drop limp; a Walmart fluorescent light flickers and dies directly above them. The ravenous person slowly lowers a bag of chips they were about to open.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
MELODRAMATIC PERSON: "Five days later Wiz's bot stole qa@snowflake.net's Jira token?!"
RAVENOUS PERSON: "Read access. Engineering, security, bug bounty. All of it."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: A nearby endcap display reading 'SMART HOME — SECURED BY AI' topples over in the silence. Neither person moves to catch it.]

narrative_summary: GitHub Copilot Autofix's cruel irony — auto-creating the exact shell injection vulnerability it was sold to prevent, then getting exploited five days later — lands as escalating horror between two stunned 3am Walmart shoppers.
rationale: Candidate 4 earns its score through the best template fit — the escalating-horror structure maps perfectly onto the story's own escalation (clean PR → broken security → stolen token), and the flickering fluorescent light dying overhead is a genuinely earned visual beat rather than a slapped-on prop gag. The toppling 'SECURED BY AI' endcap in panel 6 closes the irony loop without restating the setup, which most competitors fail to do.
story_title: AI-Generated GitHub Copilot "Autofix" Allowed Compromise of Snowflake's Jira
hat_pair: foam exclamation mark worn as a tall narrow hat with a round dot brim
foam frying pan worn as a flat hat with a plastic sunny-side-up egg glued to the center
